title: Plans travel on RTO2, never on oorexx_rto
summary: RTO2's core (AlchemyRTO, API alchemy.rto/0.1) sends state, never code: the receiver supplies an object of its own installed class, reconstruction is inert, bind and activate are separate. A NewShell Plan travels this way: the Plan class is on the MU from a digest-checked kit; only the plan's state crosses. On 24 Nov a two-process probe showed dev3 reconstruct checked nothing (wrong target, foreign schema, tampered and stale envelopes all accepted); alchemy_rto_core v0.1-dev4 (Claude (Opus 5.5)) adds admit: RTO_SCHEMA, RTO_SEQUENCE, RTO_WRONG_TARGET, RTO_STALE, RTO_DIGEST (SHA-512 over a canonical envelope), RTO_SEAL (HMAC-SHA-512 shared key, or Ed25519 where the receiver holds only public keys); lifecycle recorded. 20 checks in two processes; published 3dda4fa5, passed on Tom's host (5.3.0 r13196). The older oorexx_rto (RTOSerializer, wire label oorexx.rto.v2) rebuilds classes from shipped method source: shipped init, leaf and superclass methods ran address system on the receiver with RTOSecurityManager supplied. It must not be used between nodes.
authority: built and tested (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: Between nodes always pass a verifier: a digest alone detects damage, not an attacker
Every RTO_* refusal is fail-closed; the target is untouched
procedure: Capture with a sealer; reconstruct with a verifier; then bind and activate under the receiving policy
